batchName: Early Republic: Final Conquest of Italy (290-264 BCE) - Latin words
chapterName: Early Republic: Final Conquest of Italy (290-264 BCE)
description: Written by hand from the chapter text: the Latin words it explains

questions.question: What was the Via Appia?
options: The Appian Way, a road south from Rome
questions.explanation: It carried Roman armies and influence deep into the south, toward Capua.
questions.sourceQuote: It also built the Appian Way (*Via Appia*), a great road running south

questions.question: What does Magna Graecia mean?
questions.explanation: It was the name for the rich Greek cities of southern Italy, such as Tarentum.
questions.sourceQuote: Southern Italy was home to *Magna Graecia*, or Great Greece,

questions.question: Why are the wars with Carthage called “Punic”?
options: From Punici, the Romans’ name for the Carthaginians
From the Punic river in Africa
From a Carthaginian king named Punicus
questions.explanation: The Carthaginians were of Phoenician origin, and the Romans called them Punici.
questions.sourceQuote: "Punic" comes from *Punici*, the Romans' name for the Carthaginians

questions.question: The Hortensian law banned votes on nundinae. What were they?
questions.explanation: Banning votes on market days made it harder for country farmers, who came to town to trade, to vote.
questions.sourceQuote: it banned votes on market days (*nundinae*),

questions.question: Pyrrhus left a praesidium in Tarentum. What was it?
options: A small garrison of his soldiers
questions.explanation: The garrison was allowed to go home in peace when Tarentum fell in 272 BC.
questions.sourceQuote: leaving only a small garrison (*praesidium*) of his soldiers in Tarentum.

questions.question: What were Rome’s socii?
options: States allied to Rome that had to supply soldiers
The Greek cities Rome ruled directly
questions.explanation: They stayed independent in name but sent troops for Rome’s wars.
questions.sourceQuote: its allies (*socii*), that stayed independent in name

questions.question: What did the lex Hortensia of 287 BC do?
options: Made every decision of the Plebeian Council binding on all citizens
Gave the plebeians their own consul
questions.explanation: It removed the need for the Senate to approve plebeian decisions, ending the Conflict of the Orders.
questions.sourceQuote: made every decision (*plebiscitum*) of the Plebeian Council (*concilium plebis*) binding on all citizens

questions.question: Some communities received civitas sine suffragio. What was it?
options: Citizenship without the right to vote
questions.explanation: It was one of Rome’s tools for absorbing conquered peoples.
questions.sourceQuote: a partial version without the right to vote (*civitas sine suffragio*).
